title: Components: MCP host, client and server

videos.script: MCP names three roles. The host is the application, the client is the part of it that talks to one server, and the server offers the tools. This lesson finds each of them on this machine, as processes. {{title}} A local server is a child of its host, running as the same user. What it inherits from the host depends on the host: one library handed it four environment variables, another handed it thirty-five, the lab's three API keys among them. {{env}} The server sees only the arguments of each call, never the conversation, which is a design principle of the protocol. {{sees}} And when two servers offer a tool with the same name, the three hosts did three different things. One refused, one renamed, and one sent the call to the wrong server without saying so. {{collision}} The host is where all of that is decided, and so the host is where it has to be decided on purpose. {{last}}
